# Tier-2 Dependencies - Require Manual Review Before Merge
#
# Criteria (any match triggers tier-2):
# - New direct dependencies (not transitive)
# - Handles: network/IO, cryptography, unsafe code, financial data
# - Repo signals: <100 GitHub stars, unmaintained (>1yr), single maintainer
#
# Format:
#   crate           - tier-2, any version change needs review
#   crate=x.y.z     - PINNED, exact version required
#
# Pinned entries include: # review-date | risk-factors
# The auto-merge workflow reads this file and applies 'tier-2' label.

ibapi=3.2.0  # 2026-07-09 | Financial protocol, community-maintained, no official SDK. Reviewed 3.0.1->3.2.0: zero unsafe, no build.rs, dependency tree byte-identical vs 3.0.1 (only the version line differs), only opens a caller-supplied TWS socket + opt-in local recorder dir (IBAPI_RECORDING_DIR).
binance-sdk=60.0.0  # 2026-09-13 | Exchange SDK, signing/IO. PINNED: margin user-data stream couples to 3 `binance_sdk::common` internals (lower-stability than the public per-market API). ANY bump MUST re-verify all 3 before merge:
#   1. common::websocket::WebsocketApi::send_message      — signature + WebsocketMessageSendOptions signing fields (margin WS subscribe send)
#   2. ws.common.events.subscribe (WebsocketEventEmitter) — receive/event-callback path (margin WS event delivery)
#   3. common::utils::send_request                        — signature + HMAC signing + X-MBX-APIKEY header (hand-rolled `userListenToken` POST; SDK binds no endpoint for it)
# Background: legacy margin listen-key user-data API retired 2026-02-20; SDK binds only the dead endpoint, so the live `userListenToken` flow is hand-rolled atop these internals.
#
# Re-verified against the vendored =60.0.0 source on 2026-09-13. All 3 still hold:
#   1. `send_message(&self, method: &str, payload: BTreeMap<String, Value>,
#      options: WebsocketMessageSendOptions) -> Result<SendWebsocketMessageResult<R>, WebsocketError>`
#      — shape unchanged; the margin WS call site still matches.
#   2. `WebsocketEventEmitter::subscribe` still spawns exactly one task per subscription draining an
#      unbounded channel via `while let Some(event) = rx.recv().await { callback(event) }`, so the
#      FnMut is invoked sequentially. That is precisely the contract the non-atomic `Option::take()`
#      in the margin `account_stream` callback relies on for soundness.
#   3. `send_request(configuration, endpoint, method, query_params, body_params, time_unit, is_signed)`
#      — 7-arg shape unchanged; `is_signed` still injects `timestamp`, signs via
#      `configuration.signature_gen.get_signature(&query_params, body_ref)`, appends `signature` to the
#      query string, and sets `X-MBX-APIKEY`. The hand-rolled `POST /sapi/v1/userListenToken` is
#      therefore still signed as intended.
#
# Record gap, noted so the shape of the miss is not repeated: this entry read `=52.0.0` until
# 2026-09-13 while the manifest had already moved to `=55.0.0` (aefb55b) and then `=60.0.0` (7d8d081).
# Both were plain Dependabot bumps that changed `rustrade-execution/Cargo.toml` without touching this
# file, so the re-verification this entry mandates was never recorded for either. The check above
# closes that gap at 60.0.0. The hard `=` pin in the manifest is the enforcement; this file is the
# record. They must move together, and a bump that edits only the manifest has skipped a required step.
quick-xml  # 2026-07-08 | New direct dep (XML parsing of broker Flex statements). Reviewed @ 0.41.0: #![forbid(unsafe_code)] crate-wide, zero net-new transitive deps (serde+memchr only, both already in tree), no RUSTSEC advisories, de-facto-standard parser. Not pinned — any version bump still needs review.
parquet  # 2026-07-28 | New direct dep (Parquet decode of provider bulk exports). Reviewed @ 59.1.0 and re-verified @ 59.3.0 (2026-09-13), Apache-2.0, apache/arrow-rs (ASF-governed, ~65M downloads). MUST stay `default-features = false, features = ["zstd"]` — that is what keeps `arrow` out, and re-enabling defaults pulls arrow-array/buffer/data/schema/select/ipc, base64, brotli, flate2, lz4, snap and simdutf8 in one line. Under the pinned feature set: no build.rs; no network, process-spawn or env access anywhere in the library (the only `env::var` is in `src/bin/parquet-fromcsv.rs`, a CLI binary we do not build); 19 `unsafe` sites in the compiled paths, all in columnar decode hot spots (bit packing, RLE, byte-stream-split, bloom filter) and idiomatic for the crate class. Tree is 12 direct deps. Net-new surface, measured by diffing Cargo.lock before/after rather than eyeballed: COMPILED ON ORDINARY TARGETS — seq-macro, twox-hash, libm, num-bigint 0.5 (see below), and a second major of ahash (0.8.12, now built alongside the pre-existing 0.7.8). libm is not a new dependency edge: it arrives because parquet's tree turns on the `libm` feature of the already-present num-traits. LOCKFILE-ONLY — const-random and const-random-macro enter Cargo.lock via ahash 0.8 but are target-gated and absent from `cargo tree` on every target we ship; parquet gates ahash's `compile-time-rng` feature (the only thing that pulls const-random) on `cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")`, so they build only for wasm32. Re-check them if this workspace ever targets it -- any downstream consumer targeting wasm32 will compile const-random-macro: const-random-macro is a build-time proc-macro pulling getrandom + tiny-keccak, i.e. a compile-time RNG. ALREADY PRESENT, not new — zstd/zstd-safe/zstd-sys, chrono, bytes, hashbrown, half, num-*, getrandom, once_cell, zerocopy, tiny-keccak. Verified the arrow-free column-reader API compiles and decodes real 4-column and 7-column artifacts (370,531 rows) — the feature reduction is real, not theoretical. 59.2.0 dropped the `paste` dependency outright, which retires the RUSTSEC-2024-0436 exception this entry used to carry: `paste` is no longer in Cargo.lock at all, so there is nothing left to accept. 59.2.0 also moved parquet from num-bigint 0.4 to 0.5 (deps: num-integer + num-traits only, no new surface); 0.4.6 remains in the tree for other consumers, which `bans.multiple-versions = "warn"` permits. 59.3.0 changes the dependency set no further — its list is byte-identical to 59.2.0, and no `arrow-*` crate appears anywhere in Cargo.lock. Not pinned — any version bump still needs review, and must re-check that `arrow` has not become non-optional.
databento  # 2026-09-13 | Direct dep (historical + live market data). Meets the criteria above on three counts — network/IO, credential handling (API key via `DATABENTO_API_KEY`), and financial data — but was never listed when it was introduced; this entry closes that gap rather than recording a new dependency. Reviewed @ 0.61.0, Apache-2.0, databento/databento-rs — a first-party vendor SDK, not community-maintained, which is the opposite of the ibapi risk profile above. No build.rs. Zero `unsafe` in the `databento` crate itself. The unsafe lives one level down in `dbn` (0.69.0, Apache-2.0, no build.rs, same vendor), where a grep over src reports 133 occurrences — that count includes `unsafe impl`, `unsafe fn`, blocks and comments alike, so it over-counts distinct sites. They cluster exactly where a zero-copy wire-format decoder puts them: record_ref.rs (25), decode/dbn/fsm.rs (17), record_buf.rs (16), record/conv.rs (8), plus the sync/async encode paths. Idiomatic for the crate class, same justification parquet's 19 sites get. A further 21 occurrences in dbn's python/record.rs are NOT compiled: they sit behind dbn's opt-in `python` feature, and `pyo3` is absent from Cargo.lock — re-check if the feature set ever changes. That surface is not merely theoretical, and this is the reason to keep reading dbn's changelog and not only databento's: 0.61.0 fixes an unsound `AsRef<[u8]>` for `RecordBuf` that could yield a slice longer than the backing buffer, and a metadata count bug that made decoding read into the start of records. Treat dbn bumps as soundness-relevant. 16 direct deps (async-compression, bon, chrono, dbn, futures, hex, reqwest, serde, serde_json, sha2, thiserror, time, tokio, tokio-util, tracing, zstd), all already in the tree. Not pinned — any version bump still needs review.

# Net-new lockfile entries NOT attributable to a tier-2 crate above, recorded so the
# "measured by diffing Cargo.lock" claim in the parquet entry stays true of the whole file:
#
# rand_pcg 0.10.2 — transitive, arrives via the quinn-proto 0.11.14 -> 0.11.16 bump made for
#   RUSTSEC-2026-0185, not via any direct dependency of ours. rust-random org (same maintainers
#   as `rand`, already in tree), MIT/Apache-2.0, zero build.rs, one dependency (rand_core 0.10.1,
#   also already in tree). A PCG generator used by quinn-proto for connection-ID and timing
#   jitter — not a CSPRNG and not used as one; quinn-proto takes its cryptographic randomness
#   from `ring`/`aws-lc-rs`. No advisories. Not gated: it is transitive and does not meet the
#   direct-dependency criterion, so this is a record rather than a review requirement.
